lessons.title: Rain, Rain, Go Away
lessons.from: Lesson 2A–2B: Rain, Rain, Go Away; It's Raining, It's Pouring
lessons.changes: Paired the two traditional rain rhymes as one reading; questions rewritten with text evidence and rhyme questions; added a does-it-rhyme sort.

passage.title: Rain, Rain, Go Away
passage.text: Rain, rain, go away. Come again some other day. Little Johnny wants to play. Rain, rain, go away. It's raining, it's pouring. The old man is snoring. He went to bed and bumped his head, and he couldn't get up in the morning.

lessons.title: Jack and Jill
lessons.from: Lesson 4A and 9B: Jack and Jill; Humpty Dumpty
lessons.changes: Paired the two traditional falling rhymes as one reading; questions rewritten with text evidence, including a comparison of the two characters (RL.K.9); added a recite-and-act speaking task.

passage.title: Jack and Jill
passage.text: Jack and Jill went up the hill to fetch a pail of water. Jack fell down and broke his crown, and Jill came tumbling after. Humpty Dumpty sat on a wall. Humpty Dumpty had a great fall. All the king's horses and all the king's men couldn't put Humpty together again.

passage.text: Hickory, dickory, dock. The mouse ran up the clock. The clock struck one. The mouse ran down. Hickory, dickory, dock. Baa, baa, black sheep, have you any wool? lessons.title: The Lion and the Mouse
lessons.from: Lesson 10: The Lion and the Mouse
lessons.changes: Shortened the fable; kept waking the lion, the promise, the lion's laugh, the hunter's net, chewing the ropes and the moral; removed the 'king of beasts' exchange and the lion's change of mood; questions rewritten with text evidence, the moral tagged as a grade 1 stretch (RL.1.2); added a retelling task.

tasks.title: Read: The Lion and the Mouse

passage.title: The Lion and the Mouse
passage.text: Once upon a time, a little mouse ran across a sleeping lion. The lion woke up. He was angry! He grabbed the mouse with his big paw. “Please let me go,” said the mouse. “Someday I will help you.” The lion laughed. How could a tiny mouse help a big lion? But he let the mouse go. Not long after, the lion was caught in a hunter's net. He could not get out. The mouse heard the lion roar. He ran to the net and chewed the ropes with his sharp little teeth. Soon the lion was free! “Little friends may be great friends,” said the mouse.

lessons.title: The Dog and His Reflection

lessons.changes: Shortened the fable; kept the bone, refusing to share, the bridge, the reflection, dropping the bone and the moral; removed the butcher and burying the bone; questions rewritten with text evidence, the moral tagged as a grade 1 stretch (RL.1.2); added an opinion-writing task.

tasks.title: Read: The Dog and His Reflection

passage.title: The Dog and His Reflection
passage.text: Once upon a time, a big dog got a juicy bone. Other dogs asked, “Please let us smell your bone.” But the big dog did not want to share. He ran off to hide his bone. He came to a bridge over a stream. He looked down into the water and saw another dog with another bone! “I want that bone, too,” said the big dog. He opened his mouth to grab it. Splash! His own bone fell into the water. The other dog was only his reflection. The big dog lost his bone. If you are greedy, you may lose everything.

lessons.title: The Hare and the Tortoise
lessons.from: Lesson 12: The Hare and the Tortoise
lessons.changes: Shortened the fable; kept the boasting hare, the challenge, the hare's nap, the steady tortoise and the moral; removed the animals starting the race, the carrots and the pumpkin patch; questions rewritten with text evidence, the moral tagged as a grade 1 stretch (RL.1.2); added a fable-characters comparison (RL.K.9).

tasks.title: Read: The Hare and the Tortoise

passage.title: The Hare and the Tortoise
passage.text: There once was a hare who was very fast. He liked to tell everyone how slow they were. “You are so slow!” he said to the tortoise. “I bet I can beat you in a race,” said the tortoise. The race began. The hare ran far ahead. He looked back and saw the tortoise far behind. So the hare lay down for a nap. The tortoise kept going, slowly but steadily. The tortoise passed the sleeping hare. When the hare woke up, it was too late. The tortoise won the race! Slow and steady wins the race.
